messages.author: 9aebc57b6468b4b6
messages.subject: devtools unwanted side effects
parts:
Hello,


I already posted this question on stack overflow (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24036019/how-to-troubleshoot-devtools-unwanted-side-effects) but didnt get very far.

It's the first time I use devtools and I am running into very strange side effects after having run devtools functions like load_all().

For example, the help functions do not work anymore. But there are other very strange problems like subsetting data.table.

Here is minimalist example how I can reproduce it. Basically I start a clean R session, create an empty package and then use load_all. Once I have done that, the help function doesnt work anymore. I have put a screen capture at the end of this post, with the session info. It doesnt seem I have corrupted .data in my session. I have tried many things but cannot find the correct way to troubleshoot the problem. What would you do?


> setwd("c:/Scratch")
> require(devtools)
Loading required package: devtools

Attaching package: ‘devtools’

The following objects are masked from ‘package:utils’:

    ?, help

The following object is masked from ‘package:base’:

    system.file

> help("data.frame")
starting httpd help server ... done
> create("mypackage",rstudio=F)
Creating package mypackage in .
No DESCRIPTION found. Creating with values:

Package: mypackage
Title: What the package does (short line)
Version: 0.1
Authors@R: "First Last <first...@example.com> [aut, cre]"
Description: What the package does (paragraph)
Depends: R (>= 3.1.0)
License: What license is it under?
LazyData: true
> help("data.frame")
> load_all("mypackage")
Loading mypackage
> help("data.frame")
Error in names(t1) <- rep(names(L), lapply(L, length)) : 
  attempt to set an attribute on NULL
>> sessionInfo()
R version 3.1.0 (2014-04-10)
Platform: i386-w64-mingw32/i386 (32-bit)


attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] mypackage_0.1 devtools_1.5 

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] digest_0.6.4   evaluate_0.5.5 httr_0.3       memoise_0.2.1  parallel_3.1.0 RCurl_1.95-4.1 stringr_0.6.2  tools_3.1.0    whisker_0.3-2 
>

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: devtools unwanted side effects
parts:
It looks like you're running into a bug in the help when a package has no help files. I just pushed a fix. Since you're on Windows, see ?build_github_devtools for instructions on how to upgrade to the latest development version of devtools.

-Winston

parts:
Actually, adding a document didn't solve the other problem I have.

Here is how to reproduce it, from a fresh session

> create("mypackage",rstudio=F)

Creating package mypackage in .
No DESCRIPTION found. Creating with values:

Package: mypackage
Title: What the package does (short line)
Version: 0.1
Authors@R: "First Last <first...@example.com> [aut, cre]"
Description: What the package does (paragraph)
Depends: R (>= 3.0.2)

License: What license is it under?
LazyData: true

> document()
Updating mypackage documentation
Loading mypackage
First time using roxygen2 4.0. Upgrading automatically...
Writing NAMESPACE
Writing mypackage.Rd
> test()
Loading required package: testthat
No testing infrastructure found. Create it?

1: Yes
2: No

Selection: 1

Then I put this content int tests/testthat/test.r

require(data.table)
data.table(x=c(1,2,3))[,x]

And when I run the test command, I get the error

> test()
Testing mypackage
Loading mypackage
Error in `[.data.frame`(x, i, j) : object 'x' not found

But doing 
> source("tests/testthat/test.r")
Works ok.

I am really puzzled by these side effects! Very strange. That would be fantastic if you could have a look, thanks for the hard work.
